external_entities.name: Member
external_entities.description: A grocery loyalty programme member who uses the mobile app and may connect partner apps.

external_entities.name: Member phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone that runs the mobile app and stores its refresh token.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

processes.name: Mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application used by members to sign in and call the rewards API.

processes.name: Authorization server
processes.description: The server that signs members in, issues authorization codes and tokens, and handles consent and partner authorization.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow

processes.name: Rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger and supports gift-card redemption.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

processes.name: Partner app
processes.description: A web application operated by another company that can show a member's points.
processes.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: Browser
processes.description: A browser used by a member to sign in to the authorization server and complete partner-app authorization.
processes.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

processes.name: Support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.

data_stores.name: Identity database
data_stores.description: Database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database

data_stores.name: Points ledger
data_stores.description: Ledger holding every member's balance and every points transaction, including the client recorded for each change.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Store containing every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back.

data_flows.name: use refresh token
data_flows.description: The mobile app uses a refresh token with the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: every time the app uses it, its expiry slides forward another ninety days.

data_flows.name: disconnect partner app
data_flows.description: The mobile app requests disconnection of a partner app and deletion of its refresh token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members can disconnect a partner app from the settings screen of the mobile app

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests containing its client secret.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The browser accesses the authorization server's sign-in page and consent screen.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

data_flows.name: return authorization code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: The partner app shows a member's points through the rewards API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.

data_flows.name: get access token
data_flows.description: The support console obtains access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account. It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.

data_flows.name: manage identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server reads and writes accounts, credentials, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: Accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: manage points ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write request logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes each received request, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

trust_boundaries.name: Own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account where the platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: Members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: Members' phones, outside the organisation's cloud account.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: apart from the members' phones and the partner apps.

trust_boundaries.name: Partner app servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers operated by other companies for their partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is an internet-facing process because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is an internet-facing process because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API presents a web interface because it is described as an API and is accessed over HTTPS.
assumptions.basis: The text calls it the rewards API and states that connections use HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data because it stores member personal data, credentials, tokens, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The text lists member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data because it stores member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the ledger holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data because request headers may contain credentials or other sensitive request data.
assumptions.basis: The text states that every request, headers included, is written to the API log store.
